initial.label: initial
initial.reason: Monomer1 is a bis-glycidyl ether based on a bisphenol core (two oxirane epoxide groups provided as OCC2CO2 and OCC4CO4) to satisfy the required epoxide functionality and to appear at least twice for crosslinking. Monomer2 is 4,4'-methylenedianiline (two primary aryl amines, each as Nc... and ...N) providing at least two amine (NC-type) reactive sites. Epoxide (monomer1) and amine (monomer2) are highly compatible for thermoset curing (epoxy-amine network) and will enable extensive crosslinking to reach a moderate-to-high rubbery modulus (Er). The aromatic bisphenol backbone in monomer1 and the aromatic diamine increase network rigidity (raising Tg toward the 80 °C target), while the glycidyl linkers and methylene bridge provide some flexibility to avoid overshooting Tg. The two reactive sites per molecule on each monomer give a high but tunable crosslink density to approach the target Er (~50) while maintaining processability and synthetic plausibility.

best.label: revision_2
best.reason: Monomer1 (diglycidyl triethylene glycol-like) contains two epoxy rings (C1OC1 and C2OC2) to enable epoxy crosslinking while introducing flexible ether/aliphatic linkers (longer PEG-like chain) to lower Tg toward the 80°C target. Monomer2 is triethylenetetramine-like (NCCNCCNCCN) with multiple NC (amine) sites (appearing ≥2) to increase crosslinking density and network rigidity, raising Er toward 50 while remaining compatible with the epoxy groups. Changes address feedback: added flexible ethers to reduce Tg and increased amine functionality to raise Er; both monomers are synthetically plausible and complementary for epoxy–amine thermoset curing.
